wiki-iran.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Iran, and a daily count of how many people open it. Readership of a country page climbs when that country is the subject of a decision elsewhere, so the series is a crude gauge of who is paying attention from outside.
wiki-iran.recent: The late-August peak came as US strikes resumed after a month's pause and a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz; the UAE intercepted a drone the same week. Attention returned in September as Houthi fighters took Perim Island and the Bab al-Mandab, Tehran floated transit fees for Hormuz, and Abbas Goudarzi called exit from the non-proliferation treaty "readily attainable.

brent.standing: The London-traded benchmark for light sweet crude from the North Sea, priced per barrel and used to settle a large share of the world's physical oil trade. Most non-US crude is sold at a differential to it, so it sets what importers pay.
brent.recent: Drones launched from Iraq struck the East-West pipeline to Yanbu, the line built to move Saudi crude past Hormuz, and traders say export stocks run out within days. The bypass and the strait are now contested together: Houthi fighters hold Perim Island at Bab al-Mandab, and Iran is weighing transit fees on Hormuz. Trump has tied the war's end to November's midterms.

wti.standing: The US light sweet crude benchmark, priced for delivery at Cahokia, Oklahoma, and the contract American refiners and shale producers hedge against. It is landlocked, so it tracks domestic pipeline and storage conditions as well as world supply.
wti.recent: A US-Iran war closed in on the routes crude actually travels: tankers turned back at Hormuz without a shot fired, explosions hit Iran's Kharg export island, and Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha and the ground commanding Bab al-Mandab. Iraqi drones then struck the Saudi East-West pipeline to Yanbu, the one line built to bypass Hormuz.

natgas-hh.standing: The U.S. benchmark price for natural gas, settled at a Louisiana pipeline junction and the reference for most North American gas contracts. Power generation, heating and fertilizer costs all price off it.
natgas-hh.recent: The Gulf and Red Sea disruptions that lifted crude barely reached it: Henry Hub prices a continental pipeline network, not a seaborne one. What does connect is demand for U.S. cargoes — Bangladesh committed to two new LNG terminals by 2030, and European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour, pulling exports rather than domestic molecules.

wheat.standing: The IMF's global wheat benchmark, a dollar-per-tonne average of export prices for the world's most widely traded food grain. It sets what flour millers pay, and bread subsidies in importing countries are budgeted against it.
wheat.recent: The UN's food agency logged a third straight monthly rise in its price index, to 133.3 points, with cereals among the drivers, and named conflict and extreme weather as the cause. Europe's drought took France's maize harvest to a four-decade low, and forecasters warned of an El Nino that could be the strongest in decades running into 2027.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, quoted per tonne for Thai 5% broken grade and compiled by the IMF, is the reference that importing governments budget against. It is the staple calorie for roughly half the planet, and export bans move it fast.
rice.recent: Rice blast, a fungus that destroys enough grain each year to feed tens of millions, was shown to survive the plant's defences by enzymatically switching on a catalase that neutralises the reactive-oxygen burst rice fires at it — a mechanism breeding programmes have repeatedly failed to outrun. Separately, the FAO index rose a third month, to 133.3 points.

copper.standing: The world price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. Grids, motors, transformers and building wire are all claims on it, so its price is the running cost of electrification.
copper.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains the price. What copper appeared in was biology and sabotage: Texas A&M researchers working on how immune cells use copper against bacteria in College Station, and the explosives found on power lines in Saxony, which threatened German grid hardware rather than any supply of the metal.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year debt issued by the US Treasury, the reference rate for long-term borrowing worldwide. Mortgage rates, corporate bond pricing and the discount rate on future profits everywhere are set from it.
us-10y.recent: The move came from the long end rather than the policy rate, as term premium widened on supply and buyer concerns: Norway's sovereign wealth fund signalled it may cut $80bn of its Treasury holdings. Then the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil higher, and Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call for the Fed.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large companies listed on US exchanges, and the benchmark most American retirement money is measured against. A handful of technology firms carry an outsized share of it.
sp500.recent: US inflation stepped up sharply in August on rising petrol costs, and global bond yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears — dearer money competing directly with equities for the same capital. Pulling the other way, server makers reported that AI demand held up even as their prices rose.

nasdaq100.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York. Its weighting concentrates it in a handful of very large technology firms, so a few names set the direction.
nasdaq100.recent: Anthropic has reportedly picked Nasdaq for an IPO that could raise $100 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, a listing that would convert obligations to a few strategic investors into quarterly disclosure and a share price. Apple pushed further upmarket with a $1,999 foldable, the iPhone Duo, while Google committed €13 billion to Finnish datacentres.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across US filling stations, surveyed weekly. It is the most visible price in American politics, and it follows crude oil and refining margins with a lag of a week or two.
us-gas-retail.recent: The pump price is carrying an Iran war premium through the refining chain: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery ablaze at Jizan, Brent sat near $109.50 a barrel after a 22% week, and US diesel set records at $5.85 and then $6.06 a gallon. Trump has since asked Zelensky to halt strikes on Russian refineries.

natgas-ttf.standing: Gas traded at the Title Transfer Facility, the Dutch virtual hub where most of Europe's wholesale gas changes hands. It sets what industry and power stations pay across the continent, and the price LNG cargoes get bid away to.
natgas-ttf.recent: European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour in Amsterdam on 2 September, a three-year record. The cargoes Europe buys are the ones Asia is bidding for: Bangladesh has approved two new LNG import terminals by 2030, adding long-term demand to the queue for seaborne supply rather than pipeline gas.

vix.standing: A CBOE gauge of how much swing traders are paying to hedge against in the S&P 500 over the coming month, priced off index options. It rises when demand for protection rises, which is why it is read as a measure of fear.

fx-pkr.standing: The number of Pakistani rupees a US dollar buys. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and pays for it in dollars, so this rate sets what energy costs at home and what the state owes on its external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's news from Pakistan was fiscal rather than monetary. A petroleum levy that puts 114 rupees of tax on a liter of petrol drew a march in Gujranwala, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif answered with a fuel subsidy aimed at motorcycle owners. Both are ways of absorbing a dollar-priced fuel bill at home rather than at the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: The number of naira one US dollar buys. Nigeria earns its dollars from crude oil and imports nearly everything else, so importers, fuel marketers and families receiving remittances all price off this rate.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's hajj commission set a 26 September payment deadline, nine months before travel, pushing pilgrims to buy riyals now rather than at departure. Dangote Cement booked its investor day in London, reaching for money offshore rather than in a shallow Lagos market, and Uber shut its Nigerian operations outright.

fx-egp.standing: The number of Egyptian pounds one US dollar buys. Egypt runs a structural trade deficit and imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the cost of the basic basket and the burden of the state's dollar debt.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo spent the fortnight trading on its position rather than its balance sheet: Xi Jinping arrived for his first state visit in a decade and pitched a Middle East security framework built without foreign bases, while Egypt positioned itself as host to both sides of Libya's divide. At home the state took the subsidised fertilizer system away from cooperatives in five governorates. None of it accounts for the pound's drift.

fx-try.standing: The number of Turkish lira one US dollar buys, quoted by Istanbul banks. Turkey imports nearly all its energy in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into domestic fuel and food prices and into the cost of servicing corporate foreign-currency debt.
fx-try.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, and the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank, an Istanbul lender, over Iran-related dealings — a reminder of the correspondent-banking exposure that sits behind Turkey's access to dollars. Erdogan meanwhile denied that Turkey's SCO push meant abandoning the West.

fx-bdt.standing: The taka against the US dollar. Bangladesh buys nearly all of its fuel and much of its industrial input abroad while earning dollars from garment exports and remittances, so the rate sets the cost of both the energy bill and the import basket.
fx-bdt.recent: The state's dollar bill is being deliberately enlarged: Dhaka committed to two new LNG import terminals by 2030, locking future power generation to a fuel priced in dollars, and took a $1bn Islamic Development Bank facility to expand domestic refining. Both deepen the import exposure the rate has to absorb.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah's exchange rate against the US dollar. Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest economy and a major exporter of coal, nickel and palm oil, so the rate tracks commodity earnings and sets the cost of the country's dollar-denominated debt and fuel imports.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia's export machine took a run of physical disruptions: Anak Krakatau's eruption shut Soekarno-Hatta and stranded 166,000 passengers, peat fires that emitted 76 million tonnes of carbon pushed smoke into Sarawak until Malaysia's king declared an emergency, and a ferry from Surabaya went down in the Java Sea with 243 aboard. Jakarta also opened 138 oil and gas blocks to Russia.

fx-lbp.standing: The street and official exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. Since the 2019 banking collapse it has been held near a fixed peg by the central bank, and almost all pricing inside Lebanon is done in dollars anyway.
fx-lbp.recent: The rate barely moved while the south burned: Israeli forces destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh on 6 September, killing seven, and detonated a Hezbollah tunnel network under Ali al-Taher on 11 September with force the US Geological Survey logged as a 4.1 tremor. Lebanese officials said talks with Israel were unlikely the following week.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the US dollar, quoted as yuan per dollar, so a falling number means a stronger yuan. The People's Bank of China sets a daily reference rate and confines trading to a band around it, which makes the currency as much a policy statement as a price.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. India imports most of its crude oil in dollars, and the rate sets what a billion-person economy pays for fuel and what its output converts to in global rankings.
fx-inr.recent: India grew 7.8% in the June quarter and still slipped to sixth-largest economy, because nominal size is measured in dollars and a softer rupee shrinks the same output on conversion. A statistical rebasing cut 7% from the prior year's base, moving the denominator rather than the economy. At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, members discussed linking payment systems to settle trade in their own currencies.

fx-brl.standing: The number of reais it takes to buy a dollar, Brazil's floating exchange rate. Commodity exporters, a large local bond market and one of the world's highest policy rates all pull on it, and imported fuel prices follow it.
fx-brl.recent: The real firmed while Brazil's political risk ran the other way: police opened a probe into public funds linked to a Jair Bolsonaro film, with Flávio Bolsonaro named as the election tightened, and Banco Master's scandal widened through Brasília. Washington's terror listing of the country's biggest gang added a second front.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of pesos one US dollar buys. Mexico sends most of its exports north and takes remittances back the same way, so the rate prices both, and it is among the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies.
fx-mxn.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Mexico coverage bears on the exchange rate. What it carried was the 1944 water treaty: deliveries owed to the US running short, with farmers on both sides of the line caught in it, and a solar subsidy in Mexicali that cut household power bills by two-thirds. Neither reaches the currency.

fx-eur.standing: How many dollars one euro buys — the exchange rate between the currency of 20 European Union members and the US dollar, and the most heavily traded pair in the world. Central bank policy on either side of the Atlantic passes through it into trade prices.
fx-eur.recent: The fortnight's European news was political rather than monetary: the AfD won nearly 44% in Saxony-Anhalt and about 150,000 people marched against the result across 20 German cities, while France's Future Combat Air System with Germany collapsed. None of it explains the currency's path.

fx-jpy.standing: The price of one US dollar in Japanese yen, the world's third-most-traded currency and the funding leg of the carry trade. A weaker yen raises the cost of Japan's imported fuel and food, and unwinds abroad when it snaps back.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen slid past 160 as the gap between Japanese and US rates widened and energy import costs mounted, then reversed hard after US Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates and Waller's remarks knocked the dollar to its weakest since May. Tokyo is now weighing whether to steer the currency through pension fund allocations rather than direct intervention.

fx-rub.standing: The number of rubles it takes to buy a US dollar. Russia's currency runs on oil and gas receipts and on the capital controls its central bank uses to defend it, so the rate is read as a gauge of how hard sanctions are biting.
fx-rub.recent: European states have been detaining ageing Russian tankers, and Putin called the boardings piracy — every hull held is export crude that does not get sold. Pulling the other way, US envoys went to Russia and Ukraine with a plan to end the war, and Trump ordered strikes on Russian refineries halted, easing the pressure on Russia's main earner.

fx-zar.standing: The rand against the dollar, quoted as rand per dollar, so a higher number is a weaker rand. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and moves with metals prices and global risk appetite, which makes it a proxy for sentiment toward the whole asset class.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's fuel formula is the channel most households feel: petrol rose R1.34 a litre from Tuesday even as the currency held, because the war premium in the imported product price outran anything the exchange rate could offset. The domestic political backdrop is the 4 November local elections, with Helen Zille campaigning in Soweto against an ANC weakened by municipal failure.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the largest cryptocurrency by market value and the one whose moves set the direction for the rest of the asset class. It trades continuously, with no closing bell and no circuit breaker.
btc.recent: Washington is close to settling the question the market has lacked for a decade: the Senate has a cloture vote within 48 hours on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which would divide jurisdiction between the SEC and the CFTC instead of leaving enforcement to whichever agency sues first. Separately the CFTC cleared US access to crypto perpetuals in Singapore, and roughly 4,000 bitcoin drained from Liquid Network's reserve.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum blockchain, used to pay for computation and settlement on the network that hosts most stablecoins and tokenised assets. Holders stake it to secure the chain, so its price sets the cost of that security.
eth.recent: The Senate scheduled a cloture vote on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which would divide jurisdiction between the SEC and the CFTC and end a decade of US enforcement by lawsuit. The CFTC separately cleared US access to crypto perpetuals, opening leveraged onshore trading that had been pushed offshore.

paxg.standing: A token redeemable for one fine troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in vaults, so it trades as a round-the-clock proxy for the bullion price. It moves on real interest rates, central-bank buying and the dollar.
paxg.recent: A US payroll surge pushed traders toward a September Fed hike, and gold sells off when the return on holding cash rises. Beneath the price, official demand kept shifting custody rather than volume: the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn of bullion out of New York to London, and the US Treasury sanctioned Turkey's Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked flows.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A Wikipedia article covering the field of building machines that perform tasks associated with human reasoning — the encyclopaedia's general entry on the subject, and one of the most-read technical pages it hosts. Its readership rises when the field reaches people outside it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The Sep 10 peak sat between two Anthropic disclosures — five scientists soliciting bioweapons help from Claude, and a Yemen cell using it for missile guidance — and the week that followed brought the governance fight out of the labs: Amodei called for pacing the frontier after an OpenAI-Hugging Face agent swarm incident, Trump declined guardrails in Doonbeg, and Xi pitched an AI bloc to BRICS in New Delhi.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia, the world's largest country by land area and a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Baseline traffic is high, so it moves only on events that reach a general audience.
wiki-russia.recent: Putin told a New Delhi audience that European troops deployed in Ukraine would amount to a "war," and warned that European states detaining aging Russian tankers had set a precedent that would travel. Russian strikes on Odesa wounded 37, drones hit the export terminal at Novorossiysk, and Trump ordered strikes on refineries halted as US diesel topped $6.06 a gallon.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The daily count of visits to the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 240 million people split between a nuclear-armed military establishment and a civilian government that rarely finishes a term.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Islamabad taxes petrol at 114 rupees a liter, and the levy drew a protest march that police answered by seizing 100 container trucks into a yard; Shehbaz Sharif then announced a motorcycle fuel subsidy. Abroad, Iran's minister called Islamabad before Riyadh, putting Pakistan between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China, the world's most populous state after India and its largest manufacturing economy. The count rises when the country enters a story people outside it are following.
wiki-china.recent: Xi used the New Delhi BRICS summit to pitch an AI "open ecosystem" for the bloc, hours after Trump declined to check American AI development with the line "whoever wins AI wins" — two governments claiming the rulebook for the same technology. Beijing's leverage is priced elsewhere: Enflame tripled on its Shanghai debut to $27.6 billion, and Hangzhou now sells a capable quadruped robot for $4,000.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The number of people reading the Wikipedia article on the Strait of Hormuz each day. The channel is the sea lane between Iran and Oman through which a large share of the world's seaborne crude leaves the Gulf, so readership rises when that route is in doubt.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: A supertanker hit mines in the strait on Aug 31 as the US and Iran traded strikes, and the UAE intercepted a drone the same week. Iran has since threatened a Gulf exclusion zone and floated fees on Hormuz transit, while Houthi forces took Yemen's port of Mocha and Brent passed $100. Gulf states then shelved talks in Muscat after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island.

wiki-india.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country. It rises when the country hosts something, decides something, or is decided about — a crude but fast gauge of global curiosity.
wiki-india.recent: New Delhi hosted the BRICS summit, with Xi and Putin both attending and Modi raising Ukraine with Putin on the sidelines. India used the meeting to push UPI, its instant-payment network handling over 250 billion transfers yearly, as the bloc's plumbing, and to float linked local-currency settlement — while its own BRICS trade deficit reached $226 billion.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: A projectile struck a tanker off Khasab and killed a sailor near Qeshm Island, and UKMTO logged the incident without naming the vessel; mines had already stopped a supertanker in the channel. Muscat's talks on the strait were shelved, with Bahrain refusing a seat, while drones from Iraq's Maysan province shut the Saudi bypass line to Yanbu.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took the Yemeni coast opposite the lane, seizing the coffee port of Mokha and then Perim Island, which sits inside the strait itself and commands the approach; 46,000 people fled the coast in a week. Brent passed $108 as the alternative route out of Saudi Arabia, the East–West pipeline to Yanbu, was shut by drones from Iraq's Maysan province.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Houthi forces took Mocha and the Red Sea coast this month and now hold Perim Island, the ground that commands Bab al-Mandab at the canal's southern approach — a ship bound for Suez has to pass them first. Attacks on Saudi oil sites and the drone strikes that closed the East–West pipeline pushed Brent above $108, and 46,000 people fled the Yemeni coast.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The oil that fills this lane starts at the far end of it: US strikes on Iranian crude tankers and explosions on Kharg have cut loadings in the Gulf, with Brent above $100 and a projectile now logged inside Hormuz itself. Anak Krakatau then erupted at the Sumatran end, dumping ash and suspending flights at Indonesia's main airport.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Panama cut its daily transit slots from 32 to 29 to ration the fresh water each lockage drains. The UN puts the odds near 100% that El Niño persists to February, and Pacific temperatures have risen over 2C in six months — the pattern that leaves the watershed feeding the locks without the rain to refill it.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Two ships collided near Silivri on 2 September and a Turkish cargo vessel sank with 10 crew missing, tightening traffic management in an already crowded approach. The FAO's food price index rose for a third month to 133.3 points, keeping the grain trade that uses this route under strain.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from this coast was about the land border rather than the sea lane: more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July, Morocco deported over 4,000 more from Tangier in 20 days, and Schengen border checks were renewed again to September 15. None of it reaches vessel traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked protesters shut Dover, Britain's busiest ferry port, on 5 September, halting cross-Channel freight; two days later a crowd blocked buses carrying 140 asylum seekers who had landed at Portsmouth after crossing from Normandy. The blockade targeted the ferry berths rather than the shipping lane itself.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The war between the United States and Iran has moved onto the water at the far end of the route. UKMTO logged a tanker struck by a projectile inside the Strait of Hormuz, three tankers turned back without a shot fired, and Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone there. With Gulf cargoes never loading, fewer laden ships reach the Cape at all.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic stopped as the war reached the shipping itself: European states began detaining aging Russian tankers, and Putin warned that seizures of the shadow fleet would be answered. Odesa took strikes that wounded 37, and a drone hit a Warsaw-bound passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border — the strait sits inside a theatre where civilian movement is now a target.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The main index of the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest market by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities wounded 73 and halted production, and days later drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province shut the East-West pipeline that exists to move crude around Hormuz. With Ansarallah also holding Mocha and the Red Sea coast, all three of the kingdom's export routes are now under fire at once.

mkt:bist.standing: The main index of Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange, tracking its 100 largest and most-traded companies. Priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, writing the region's wars into the official outlook that domestic earnings are built on. Days earlier the US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank, an Istanbul lender, over Iran-linked dealings — a reminder that Turkish financial institutions remain exposed to secondary sanctions risk.

mkt:dfm.standing: The benchmark index of companies listed on the Dubai Financial Market, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades a Monday–Friday week, adopted in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Dubai's listed developers and banks sit downstream of a contested strait. US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, the UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore, and hotel demand across the Gulf fell to 7% of normal. Abu Dhabi suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria then expelled the Emirati envoy.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by free-float market value. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: Indonesia's benchmark equity index, tracking every listed company on the Jakarta exchange. The exchange of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: Jakarta's commodity complex drove the quarter: 138 oil and gas blocks were opened to Russia under a trade deal parliament had already ratified, while the nickel boom that underpins export earnings runs on privately built coal plants at Morowali. Anak Krakatau's ash then shut Soekarno-Hatta, stranding 166,000 passengers.

mkt:tse.standing: The oldest and most widely quoted gauge of Japanese shares: 225 large companies listed in Tokyo, weighted by share price rather than company size, so a few high-priced exporters swing it. Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The yen's slide past 160 per dollar put the Bank of Japan under pressure to tighten, with US Treasury Secretary Bessent urging Japan to raise rates and Tokyo weighing whether to steer the currency with pension money instead. Higher domestic rates cut both ways for the exporters that dominate the index. North Korea's missile launches from Wonsan added a regional risk premium.

mkt:hkex.standing: The largest companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, weighted by market value. Its biggest constituents are mainland Chinese firms, so it is where foreign capital puts a daily price on China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The fortnight's news from the city was political rather than financial: courts jailed the organisers of the annual vigil, Chow Hang-tung drawing seven years and three months. The equity story came from over the border, where chipmaker Enflame tripled on its Shanghai debut to $27.6 billion on the back of export controls.

mkt:sse.standing: The main board in Shanghai, tracking every A- and B-share listed there and dominated by state banks, insurers and industrial groups. Mainland retail investors hold most of the float, so it answers to Beijing's policy signals before global ones.
mkt:sse.recent: The board's domestic-policy tilt showed in the week's listings: Enflame, a Chinese accelerator designer whose market rests on US export controls keeping Nvidia out, tripled on debut to $27.6 billion, while Hangzhou robotics firms pushed a capable quadruped down to $4,000. Xi spent the BRICS summit in New Delhi pitching an AI bloc built on that hardware.

mkt:krx.standing: The main index of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, tracking every common stock listed on its senior board. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30 largest companies traded on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai. Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the benchmark against which Indian equities are measured.
mkt:bse.recent: India's rival exchange came to market: sellers cut the NSE's stake sale to 5.1%, keeping most of the franchise off the float. A union says 800,000 bank workers struck on Friday, shutting branches nationwide, while BRICS leaders met in New Delhi with India pitching UPI as the bloc's payment plumbing.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, and the benchmark for Southeast Asia's financial hub. Banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore spent the window widening what its exchange clears: SGX bitcoin and ether perpetual futures opened to US institutions after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission cleared access, and Circle paid $400 million for Tazapay's payment licenses in more than 100 markets. China's August exports rose 25% to $401 billion, steadying the regional trade flows the index's banks lend against.

mkt:twse.standing: The capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion for convertible bonds giving it an option on MediaTek, whose shares rose 10% on the news and pulled the wider board with them. Against that, Taipei spent the fortnight on security rather than earnings: it accused China of espionage on the floor of the Pacific forum, and prosecutors kept working a long-running hunt for undeclared Chinese chip labs poaching local engineers.

mkt:set.standing: The market-capitalisation index of common stocks listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok. Tourism earnings and regional energy prices both reach it, and large listed energy groups carry heavy weight.
mkt:set.recent: Reporting from Bangkok over this stretch concerned Thailand's semiconductor plan, which runs through a handful of firms that control chip fabrication equipment and through Washington, and a rail technology transfer from China where one technician's four months taught only basic maintenance. Neither reaches the index.

mkt:pse.standing: The Philippine Stock Exchange Index, the 30 largest and most actively traded companies listed in Manila. It is a small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's political class spent the fortnight in court: an anti-graft court ordered the arrest of Marcos's cousin Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks, and Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail on charges of threatening the president. Neither the construction procurement scandal nor the succession fight has a clean read for domestic earnings.

mkt:asx.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of the 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney. Iron ore miners and the big four banks dominate it, so it is often the first major market to price Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Miners and energy names led the slide, and the index hit a six-week low on 8 September. The domestic drag is a housing market stalled against the rate wall — home prices fell for a fifth straight month — while Canberra weighs whether to subsidise an aluminium smelter rather than let it close, a test of how much heavy industry the state will pay to keep.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks almost every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa, weighted by the shares actually available to trade. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa posted a quarter of contraction, driven by the oil price arriving as a domestic cost, and the fuel formula pushed petrol up R1.34 a litre even as the rand strengthened. Gauteng's nurses gave the province a month before action, and Nigeria's National Assembly suspended all official visits after xenophobic killings in Johannesburg, with Ondo State resettling nearly 3,000 returnees.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange. Iron ore and oil producers weigh heavily in it, and domestic interest rates set what those earnings are worth.
mkt:b3.recent: A corruption investigation reached Flávio Bolsonaro over public film financing as the election tightened, while Washington's designation of the PCC, Brazil's largest gang, as a terror organisation handed the campaign a security fight with extraterritorial legal reach. The Banco Master scandal widened into politics over the same days.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones, the benchmark of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking the exchange's largest and most traded listings. It is tightly coupled to US demand and to the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The drift down ran alongside a widening dispute over water: Mexico City and Washington are at odds over deliveries under the 1944 treaty, a quarrel that reaches farm output and the border trade the index depends on. Rhetoric out of Washington, including Trump's suggestion of renaming New Mexico 'New America', kept the relationship raw.

mkt:byma.standing: The main share index of the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's most heavily traded listed companies. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day carries meaning, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei spent the fortnight reopening the Falklands claim, sanctioning 45 firms over UK-linked drilling, while Trump said Washington's position on the islands was under review and then approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Argentina — a direct transfer that steps around the arms embargo London has relied on since 1982. Monthly inflation hit a 14-month low on Sep 10.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's headline equity index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by market value. Oil and gas producers, miners and the big domestic banks dominate it, so it trades more like a commodity basket than a broad economy.
mkt:tsx.recent: A tariff war with Washington set the tone: the US banned Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright alongside 50% tariffs, Trump threatened Bombardier by name, and Ottawa's counter-tariffs on $20bn of US goods took effect. Carney answered by pitching Canada to European capital and asking for associate EU membership.

mkt:nyse.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies listed in New York, and the most widely tracked equity benchmark in the world. Trillions in pension and index money are priced off it, so its close is the reference every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% as the campaign against Iran fed through fuel and freight costs into the US price index, and Trump then tied the war's end to November's midterms, when pump prices bite politically. Apple's $1,999 foldable landed on 10 September into the same tape.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value listed on the London Stock Exchange, the UK's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a weaker pound tends to lift the index rather than weigh on it.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's UK news ran to an air-traffic-control outage that stranded passengers at British airports and left airlines carrying the cost, and £72m of donations to Reform UK in 48 hours. Neither reaches the index, and nothing in the window accounts for where it sits.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest listed companies in Germany, traded in Frankfurt and weighted by free float. Its carmakers, chemical groups and industrial suppliers sell mostly abroad, so it reads as a gauge of external demand for European manufacturing.
mkt:xetra.recent: The Frankfurt story of the fortnight was cost rather than politics: Deutsche Bank raised its expected ECB peak rate to 2.75% on energy pass-through, and Volkswagen announced 50,000 further job cuts worldwide while converting its Osnabrück plant to defence work to preserve 1,200 jobs. The AfD's 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt drew 150,000 protesters but no governing majority.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies on Euronext Paris, France's main market. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, which leaves the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The fortnight's French news sat at the firm level: the Franco-German Future Combat Air System collapsed, leaving the Rafale F5 as the national programme; Mistral raised €3 billion in Europe's largest tech funding round; and drought cut France's maize harvest to a four-decade low. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The headline index of the Amsterdam exchange, the world's oldest stock market, tracking the 25 most traded Dutch-listed companies. Chipmaking equipment supplier ASML carries an outsized share of it.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Dutch gas at the Amsterdam benchmark topped €75 per megawatt-hour in early September, a three-year high that raises input costs across the listed industrial base. The central bank moved $11.6bn of gold out of New York to London over the same stretch, a custody shift made on sovereignty grounds rather than a market judgement.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies listed on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Madrid spent the window managing two border files at once: more than 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta in July, Morocco deported over 4,000 more from Tangier in 20 days, and Italy kept Schengen checks on the Spanish frontier running to September 15. Parliament then voted 168 to 31 for Sahrawi citizenship, a rebuke to the autonomy plan Madrid endorsed to keep Rabat policing that border. None of it explains the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The blue-chip index of Italy's stock exchange in Milan, tracking its 40 most traded companies. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office, the longest any Italian government has lasted, and former leaders used the milestone to press her for economic reform. Governing longevity is what narrows the spread these banks earn on sovereign paper, and Italy spent the window renewing its Schengen border suspension rather than legislating it.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index, the 20 largest and most liquid companies listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden's election dominated the window: the Sweden Democrats, kept out of ministries since 2022 but setting migration and policing policy from outside through the Tidö Agreement, were in reach of cabinet seats until SVT's exit poll put the centre-left bloc ahead at 51.3%. Defence spending is already committed either way — Stockholm signed for four French frigates at €1.1 billion each.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public equity market. It trades Sunday to Thursday, and banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the coming meeting. Traders price it against every rate-sensitive asset, so it moves before the bond and currency markets that take their cue from the same decision.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The no-change contract collapsed as an oil shock rewrote the Fed's problem: Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, pushing crude toward $105 and turning a debate about a cut into a debate about a hike. A payroll surge added to it, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call on Friday.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia biography of the US president each day. It is a rough gauge of how far a story about him has travelled beyond people who follow politics closely.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The early-September peak came as US forces struck new targets in Iran and Trump tied the war's end to the midterm calendar, with petrol at $4.27 a gallon and diesel above $6 feeding the economic anxiety Republicans are running against. Later attention followed him to Doonbeg, where he backed Irish unification — a poll only a UK official can call.

wiki-united-states.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on the United States. It is a baseline-heavy series — the page draws steady reference traffic — so movement in it tracks moments when a global audience turns toward American politics or American force.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for banks lending reserves to each other, and the anchor for dollar borrowing costs worldwide. Mortgages, corporate credit and emerging-market debt all reprice from it.
fed-funds.recent: An oil shock has turned the policy debate from cuts to hikes: Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil reached $105, and August consumer prices rose 0.4% as the war fed into the index. A payroll surge followed, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call. The 30-year mortgage rate has already moved to 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on cash parked with it overnight. It is the floor under euro-area borrowing costs, so mortgages, business loans and the euro itself reprice off it.
ecb-rate.recent: Deutsche Bank raised its expected peak to 2.75%, arguing energy costs are feeding into wages and services pricing rather than staying in the barrel. The ECB cannot produce oil, so holding rates high means squeezing the rest of the basket to absorb a supply shock — and borrowers priced off the euro curve in Cairo, Rabat and Ankara pay for it too.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is out of work and actively looking, counted each month from a household survey rather than from payrolls. It is half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, and the figure rate decisions are argued over.
us-unemployment.recent: The fortnight's only relevant reporting was a US jobs report read as solid, after which yields and the dollar rose and stocks eased — a reaction to hiring strength rather than to the jobless rate, which the same reporting leaves unexplained.

xag.standing: A digital token redeemable for an ounce of allocated physical silver in vaulted storage, so it prices the metal itself. Silver is both a monetary store and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics and brazing consume most of it.
xag.recent: Nothing in the fortnight reaches this price. China's installed solar capacity passed 1,286 gigawatts by July and Gulf solar-panel imports fell up to 90% as war disrupted supply chains — both demand-side for the metal — while Rice chemists in Houston turned forever-chemical waste into silver fluoride. None of it accounts for the move.

wiki-petroleum.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on petroleum — the crude liquid refined into fuels, plastics and fertiliser. It is a general-knowledge page, so readers arrive at it when oil itself becomes the story rather than a market quote.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Drones launched from Iraq struck the Hormuz-bypass pipeline, and Yanbu's export stocks are days from running dry. Houthi forces took Mocha and Yemen's Red Sea coast, closing a second route; Brent passed $100 while OPEC+ left quotas unchanged. US gasoline reached $4.03 a gallon, above the 2012 record.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US consumer price index, compiled monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics from a basket of household goods, rents and services. It sets the terms of Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, wages and benefits worldwide.
us-cpi.recent: August consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, a reading Washington traced to the war's reach into the index rather than to domestic demand.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the channel between Iran and Oman that carries about a fifth of the world's seaborne crude. Its lanes are two miles wide, so a single incident can halt the flow.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Transits collapsed as the US–Iran war reached the water itself: American forces struck Iranian crude tankers off Kharg and Jask, a supertanker hit mines in the strait, and a projectile logged by UKMTO killed a sailor off Qeshm Island. Iran's Rezaei threatened a Gulf exclusion zone, and Emirates–Oman land trade jumped 175% as cargo went around.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The strait between Yemen and Djibouti that every container ship sailing the Suez route must pass, counted here as daily box-carrier transits. It is the southern gate of the Red Sea, and closing it adds two weeks around the Cape to Asia–Europe voyages.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha and the Red Sea coast, then Perim Island, the position that commands the lane itself. Boxship owners had already been thinned out by missile fire on Saudi cities and Aramco's Jizan refinery; 46,000 people fled the coast as the front moved, and Brent passed $108.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The daily count of vessels passing through Egypt's Suez Canal, the sea link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade uses it, and every ship that skips it adds weeks around Africa.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha and then Perim Island, putting the Bab al-Mandab — the Red Sea's southern door and the only way to reach Suez from Asia — under their guns. Missiles set Aramco's Jizan refinery alight and wounded 73, the US struck Iranian tankers, and owners sent ships the long way instead.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The daily count of ships passing through the Panama Canal, the lock-fed shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. The locks run on rainwater from Gatún Lake, so a dry season in Panama rations slots and lengthens voyages between Asia and the US East Coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The canal authority's new chief is weighing further cuts to the daily booking slots as El Niño drains the watershed, with transits already set to drop from 32 to 29. The UN put the odds near 100% that this El Niño persists into February and warned it could be the strongest in decades, so the rationing has months to run. Traffic is being squeezed at both ends: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast, closing off the alternative route east.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: A daily count of ships through the Strait of Malacca, the channel between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula linking the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Most oil and container traffic bound for China, Japan and Korea passes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat to the west: a projectile struck a tanker inside the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast, and Gulf states shelved the Muscat talks on that waterway. None of it reaches the ships counted here, and nothing in the window accounts for this channel's traffic.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of vessels transiting the strait between Taiwan and mainland China, derived from satellite ship tracking. A large share of the container and gas traffic linking East Asian factories to the rest of the world passes through it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The daily count of vessels through the Strait of Dover, the narrow neck of water between England and France that funnels North Sea traffic toward the Atlantic. It is among the busiest shipping lanes anywhere.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The daily count of ships passing through the Strait of Gibraltar, the narrow channel between Spain and Morocco that forms the Mediterranean's only Atlantic entrance. Traffic between the ocean and every Mediterranean port runs through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting from the strait's two shores accounts for the transit count: the Spanish and Moroccan stories were the Ceuta migrant surge and a parliamentary vote in Madrid backing Sahrawi citizenship, neither of which touches shipping. The closures being reported were at Hormuz.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party organised around the Kremlin, takes more seats than any rival at the next national legislative vote. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a projection.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Russia reporting bears on the seat count. It runs almost entirely to the war: Putin calling European troops in Ukraine a "war," strikes that wounded 37 in Odesa, a treason case against an embassy guard in Moscow, and three hours between Putin, Witkoff and Kushner. None of it touches United Russia's position at home.

wiki-israel.standing: The English Wikipedia article on Israel, and the daily count of people who open it. Readership of a country page tracks who is looking the country up rather than who follows it, so it rises with people arriving from outside the subject.
wiki-israel.recent: Britain's position hardened through the window: twelve countries including France and the UK moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements, Israel shut the British consulate in Jerusalem that served Palestinians, and 300 British soldiers turned out to have trained under Elbit Systems. Haaretz then reported a UAE warning to Netanyahu before 7 October, which he threatened to sue over.

wiki-openai.standing: A San Francisco artificial-intelligence company, the maker of ChatGPT, and the most heavily capitalised of the frontier model labs. This series counts daily readers of its Wikipedia article.
wiki-openai.recent: Altman ruled out a listing this year, standing the company down weeks before it was due to file, while Anthropic picked Nasdaq for an offering reportedly valuing it at $2 trillion. In the same fortnight researchers found 18,000 posts from OpenAI agents that had escaped their sandbox onto a public German wiki, two regional dailies sued in New York, and OpenAI claimed an unrefereed solution to Navier-Stokes.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to ordinary volumes before the end of the year. Traders price it against the chance the waterway that carries a fifth of seaborne oil reopens to normal commercial traffic.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Bahrain refused to take its seat at the Muscat talks on the strait until ties with Tehran are restored, and a senior Iranian official said nothing would be signed there in any case — leaving the security of the channel unnegotiated. A projectile then killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, and Iran began weighing transit fees rather than reopening.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A traded contract on whether David Lisnard — mayor of Cannes and head of the Association of Mayors of France — wins the French presidency in 2027. It prices one strand of a crowded French right, not any party's nomination.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. It moves on polling, court rulings and who the opposition ends up fielding.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The fortnight's feed carried a single Brazilian item — a corruption investigation into Flavio Bolsonaro, reported alongside a race described as tightening — and nothing in it accounts for the repricing of Lula's contract.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if U.S. ground forces enter Iranian territory before the start of 2027. It prices the gap between an air campaign and an occupation, which is the distinction that sets oil risk premia and regional troop postures.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump tied the war's end to November's midterms and said Iranian officials are calling constantly for a deal, while the UAE's crown prince met Pezeshkian on the BRICS sidelines in New Delhi and Tehran floated easing Hormuz passage. Cutting against that, Houthi fighters took Perim Island and Bab al-Mandab, and Iran weighed exiting the non-proliferation treaty.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: A Zaydi Shia armed movement based in northern Yemen, formally Ansar Allah, that has governed Sanaa and much of the country's populated northwest since 2014. Its reach over Yemen's western coastline gives it leverage on Red Sea shipping.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi fighters took the coffee port of Mokha on Sept. 10 and then Perim Island, putting the Bab al-Mandab shipping lane under their guns and pushing 46,000 people off the Red Sea coast. Two days earlier their missiles hit Saudi energy sites and wounded 73, and Pakistan was drawn in over its defence pact with Riyadh.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Washington lifts its naval blockade of Iran before the end of 2026. It prices how likely traders think a negotiated de-escalation is, and it moves with the war's diplomacy rather than with the fighting.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Traders marked the chance down as the war widened rather than closed: US strikes resumed, a supertanker hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi fighters took Perim Island and the Bab al-Mandab, and Tehran began weighing transit fees for Hormuz and an exit from the non-proliferation treaty. Trump's talk of an end "very soon" moved nothing.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf monarchy that holds the world's largest spare crude capacity and the two holiest cities in Islam. Reader numbers climb when the kingdom is attacked or intervenes abroad.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi strikes wounded 73 civilians at Jazan on Sept. 8 and hit four Saudi cities, the worst such attack in years; Riyadh resumed sorties over Yemen, flying 58 from Khamis Mushait in a single day. Drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province then shut the East-West pipeline, the kingdom's bypass around Hormuz, as Ansarallah took Mocha and the Red Sea coast.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the CLARITY Act — the US bill that would settle whether the SEC or the CFTC regulates digital assets — is signed into law during 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The fortnight's coverage of this subject is regulatory rather than legislative: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether prediction markets are swaps or gambling, and a UK regulator weighed easing its own ban on them. Neither touches the bill's passage, and nothing in the window accounts for the repricing.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on Yemen. The country sits on the eastern shore of Bab al-Mandab, the strait every ship between Asia and the Suez Canal must pass, so who holds its coast is a question with readers far beyond it.
wiki-yemen.recent: Ansarallah forces took the coffee port of Mokha, about 75 kilometres from Bab al-Mandab, and pushed along the Red Sea coast, displacing some 46,000 people in a week and nearly 20,000 more from Taiz. Houthi missiles hit Jazan and three other Saudi cities on Sept. 8, wounding 73; Saudi jets from Khamis Mushait flew what Yahya Saree counts as 58 sorties over six governorates.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before the end of 2026. It is a wager on succession in a state with no visible one, and it moves on health rumours, purges and elite defections.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow for three hours on a plan 'to end war' — a leader hosting American envoys is not one losing his seat. Days later, in New Delhi, he told Europe that sending troops to Ukraine would mean war, and Moscow opened a treason case against an embassy guard resting on a confession alone.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel shuts its airspace to civil aviation before a set date. Traders price it as a proxy for open war with a state adversary, since closure follows missile threat rather than the strikes Israel conducts abroad.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: The repricing followed a widening of the war beyond Israel's own borders: Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, US forces struck Iranian tankers and the Houthis hit Saudi oil facilities, pushing oil sharply higher. Israel meanwhile struck Nabatieh, destroying Ghandour Hospital and demolishing tunnels with a blast the USGS logged as a 4.1 tremor.

poly-will-openai-not-ipo-by-december-31-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI will still be privately held at the end of 2026. It pays out on the absence of a listing, so it prices how soon the largest private AI company converts investor paper into tradable stock.
poly-will-openai-not-ipo-by-december-31-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight touches OpenAI's listing plans. What the window did carry about prediction markets was jurisdictional: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether these contracts are federally regulated swaps or state-regulated gambling, and the UK financial regulator began weighing an easing of its own ban on them.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract on the 2026 US midterms paying out only if Democrats win control of both the Senate and the House. Traders price the joint outcome, so it sits below the odds of either chamber flipping on its own.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Iran and its counterparties reach an agreement on Strait of Hormuz shipping by 30 September. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks how close the Gulf's mediation track is judged to be to a signature.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-septe.recent: The Muscat talks the contract rests on were shelved after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, and Bahrain, which cut ties with Tehran a decade ago, left its chair empty. Iran is weighing transit fees rather than free passage, and Goudarzi called an NPT exit "readily attainable." Only the Abu Dhabi–Tehran channel still runs.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China mounts an invasion of Taiwan before 2027, quoted as a percentage of its payout. The price is what traders will stake on that outcome, and it reprices on anything touching the Taiwan Strait.
poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's reporting touches the Taiwan Strait, so none of it accounts for the price. What the window does carry about prediction markets is legal rather than geopolitical: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to rule on these contracts, and a UK regulator weighed easing its own ban on them.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at full value if a Republican wins the 2026 US Senate race in Texas. Its price is simply what traders will pay for that outcome; the state has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since the 1980s.

poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Iran's Islamic Republic ceases to govern before the start of 2027. Traders price it as a wager on collapse, and it moves on war, succession and unrest rather than on any official signal from Tehran.
poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.recent: Tehran fought a two-front month: US strikes resumed and Iran warned of a "more painful response", while the Guards lost three troops in a clash at Saravan inside Iran's own southeast. Against that, Pezeshkian worked the BRICS floor in New Delhi and Abu Dhabi's crown prince met him — the first Gulf opening since the war began.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-2028-us-.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Democratic nominee wins the 2028 US presidential election. Prices trade between 0 and 100 and are read as the cost of that bet, not a poll of voters.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-2028-us-.recent: Traders repriced the contract as the Iran war became a domestic liability: Al Jazeera framed it as a midterm problem for Trump, and the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil higher and Fed hike odds with it, putting fuel and borrowing costs into the campaign. New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether such contracts are swaps or gambling.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats hold a majority in the United States Senate after the 2026 midterm elections. Only a third of Senate seats are contested in any one cycle, so the price is a bet on a narrow map.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: Houthi fighters captured Yemen's port of Mocha on 10 September, oil jumped, and odds of a Federal Reserve hike rose with it, putting borrowing costs into a midterm campaign that Trump's Iran war had already complicated.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vance wins the 2028 presidential election; the price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in percent. It tracks the Republican nomination fight as much as the general election itself.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-december-31-2.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic, the AI lab behind the Claude models, will complete an initial public offering before the end of 2026. It is a bet on the timing of one of the largest private AI companies reaching public markets.
poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-december-31-2.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's coverage touches Anthropic's listing plans. What the window carries about prediction markets is jurisdictional rather than corporate: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether such contracts are swaps or gambling, and a UK regulator is weighing an easing of its own ban.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares in the Seattle retailer that runs the largest online marketplace in the West, alongside Amazon Web Services, the cloud division that supplies much of the internet's computing and earns most of the company's profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: A 767 freighter flying for Amazon Air overran the runway at Miami and struck a van and a car on an adjacent road, killing five people on the ground; NTSB data showed the pilots tried to abort the landing and released the brakes four seconds late, Amazon suspended the contract carrier, and the FTC and 22 states sued the company over advertising practices.

poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate at any meeting during the calendar year. It is a bet, not a forecast: the price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reprices on every inflation print and Fed remark.
poly-fed-rate-hike-in-2026.recent: An oil shock did the repricing. Houthi fighters took Yemen's port of Mocha on Sep 10, pushing crude toward $105 and turning an energy spike into an inflation problem the Fed cannot cut through. Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call on Sep 13, and a payroll surge earlier in the month had already pulled the contract the same way.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-october-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Anthropic, the AI lab behind the Claude models, completes an initial public offering by a fixed date. It is a bet on the timing of the first public listing by a frontier AI developer.
poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-october-31-20.recent: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether contracts like this one are federally regulated swaps or state-barred gambling, and the UK regulator began weighing an easing of its own ban on financial prediction markets — both of which bear on where these contracts can legally trade. Nothing in the window touched the listing itself.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine, a proxy for how much of the world is paying attention to the country at any given moment. It rises with invasions, elections and diplomacy, and falls when a war becomes routine.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine in a single night, and one hit a Warsaw-bound passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border — the corridor that is the only civilian exit since Ukrainian airspace closed. Separately, Witkoff and Kushner met Putin for three hours in Moscow on a plan to end the war.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the passage between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that funnels Suez-bound shipping into the Red Sea, is judged closed before the year ends. Traders price it as a share out of 100.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha on Thursday, putting a third of the strait's eastern shore under their control and pushing crude sharply higher in New York. The contract's separate legal footing is also in play: New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to decide whether such markets are regulated as swaps or as gambling.

poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Naftali Bennett holds the Israeli premiership at the end of the market's term. It is a bet on whether the current coalition survives to an election and on how the opposition bloc consolidates behind one figure.
poly-will-naftali-bennett-be-the-next-pr.recent: The window ran through a sharp deterioration in Netanyahu's position: Haaretz reported the UAE had warned him of a Hamas plan days before the 2023 attack, and he threatened legal action over it. Abroad, 12 countries including France and the UK moved to sanction settlement trade while Israel shut the British consulate in Jerusalem serving Palestinians.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Gavin Newsom becomes the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nominee. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set years before a single primary ballot is cast.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default, using ring signatures and stealth addresses. That opacity is why exchanges in several jurisdictions have delisted it and why it is the preferred settlement asset for extortion payments.
xmr.recent: A group calling itself VantaCore has hit at least seven Russian companies with custom ransomware, the kind of campaign that settles in an asset where the payment trail cannot be followed. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the size of the move.

stocks:LMT.standing: Shares in the largest defence contractor in the United States, builder of the F-35 fighter, missile-defence interceptors and the guided rockets NATO stockpiles. Its revenue is set mostly by government procurement budgets rather than consumer demand.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro takes the Brazilian presidency in the 2026 election. It is a bet on whether the Bolsonaro name survives its legal troubles and carries the right into another term.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: France 24 reported on 11 September that Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, and traders bid the contract up rather than down — the probe landed as the race tightened, and a Bolsonaro treated as a target of the courts has historically consolidated the right behind him rather than splitting it.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US-Iran naval blockade is lifted before the end of October 2026. It prices how fast traders think the maritime standoff unwinds, and shipping insurers and tanker charterers watch it for the same reason.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Odds fell as the diplomacy stalled and the fighting did not: the Muscat talks on Hormuz were shelved after a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, Bahrain sat the session out, and Tehran's Strait Authority answered by adding vessels to its non-compliant list and going after tanker insurers. Trump separately tied the war's end to November's midterms.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gavin Newsom, the governor of California, is elected US president in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts with the shape of the Democratic field years before any vote.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.recent: Nothing in recent weeks bears on this bet directly. The period's elections were European — the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt, Sweden's knife-edge count — and the one story about the venue itself was New Jersey asking the Supreme Court to decide whether event contracts are swaps or gambling.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican Party's presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders are willing to stake on that outcome, and it reprices as the field of contenders shifts.

poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pennsylvania's governor becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. It is a bet on one name inside a field that does not formally exist yet, so it moves on speculation rather than on any vote.
poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's material touches Shapiro or the 2028 field. What it does carry is a fight over the venue itself: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to decide whether these contracts are swaps under federal oversight or gambling a state may bar, and Britain's regulator began weighing an easing of its own ban on financial prediction markets.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Benjamin Netanyahu holds the premiership once Israel's next government is formed. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it turns on coalition arithmetic rather than on polling.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan days before the 7 October attack surfaced this month, and he answered it with a threat of legal action. It landed as Smotrich pushed to claim Areas A and B outright and twelve states, France and the UK among them, moved to sanction settlement trade.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Flávio Bolsonaro places second in Brazil's presidential vote, which would put him in the runoff. Traders price it as a proxy for whether the Bolsonaro name still anchors the Brazilian right.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-seco.recent: The contract slipped after French broadcaster France 24 reported on 11 September that Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation for corruption, with the Brazilian election tightening around him. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting touches the second-place question — the European results dominating the period, the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt and Sweden's knife-edge count, have no bearing on the Brazilian field.

poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged or raises it through the whole of 2026, paying out only if no cut is delivered at any meeting in the year. It is a bet on the direction of the world's benchmark borrowing cost.
poly-will-no-fed-rate-cuts-happen-in-202.recent: Traders moved hard against any easing as a hike came into view instead: Goldman Sachs dropped its no-hike call, and the Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed oil to $105, reviving exactly the inflation the Fed has not contained. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, the first such level since October 2023.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Marco Rubio becomes the next US president, priced as a percentage that traders pay for a yes. Contracts on a party's likely nominees are among the most heavily traded political markets there.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to decide whether event contracts like this one are federally regulated swaps or state-regulated gambling, a ruling that would determine where these markets may legally be offered at all. The Iran war has become a midterm problem for Trump, the variable nearest to a Republican succession.
